_how_to_use: PASTE ONLY THE `prompt` FIELD INTO THE IMAGE MODEL. Nothing else in this file is for the model. Pasting the whole file produced a collage of several captioned slides, because `renditions_wanted` lists two sizes, `framing.aspect_ratios` lists two ratios, and headline_in_app / caption_in_app are text - the model read all of that as a brief to draw multiple frames with words on them. Those fields are for the render pipeline and for whoever writes the app copy.
_source_image_note: Save the image you keep in this folder named `02_welcome_2_know_where_you_stand` with whatever extension the model gave you - .jpg, .png, .jpeg and .webp are all accepted. Only the NAME has to match this file; the extension does not. lessons/scripts/tutor_images.py then renders it to renders/02_welcome_2_know_where_you_stand/ as slide_1080x1920 (9:16 phone slide) and card_1080x1350 (4:5). Renditions are always written as PNG regardless of the source format.
audience: the learner setting up their own account
caption_in_app: A quick check before and after each class shows what you already know - no pressure, just progress.
intent: the small moment of a quick check landing right - seated at a table mid-study, not lounging with a phone
prompt: A single photograph, one continuous scene, filling the whole frame. Close three-quarter view of a Coloured South African girl of about 16 in a plain school-uniform shirt, seated upright at a small fold-out table in the corner of a flat's lounge, a two-plate stove and a curtained window behind her - a different home from the other slides, working through a short quiz on a phone held in both hands at chest height, screen angled away from camera so nothing on it is readable. An open exercise book and a pen lie on the table just in front of them, in frame. The expression is the point: a small private moment of 'I know this one' - mouth just starting to move, eyes steady. Soft daylight from a window to one side, the room behind softly out of focus.
negative_prompt: any text, letters, numbers, words, signage, logos, watermarks, user-interface elements, phone screens showing apps, charts or graphs, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, plastic sheen, cinematic colour grade, film still look, motion blur, lens flare, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted faces, stock-photo smiles, American classrooms, generic 'African' styling, collage, multiple panels, split screen, side-by-side frames, contact sheet, grid of images, storyboard, several phone mockups, device frames, app screenshots, before-and-after, picture-in-picture, borders, margins, framed print, bed, duvet, bedding, sitting on a bed, bedroom, lying down, slouching, idle scrolling, recreational phone use, shirtless, bare chest, bare back, no shirt, undressed, pyjamas

_pipeline_only._note: NOT model input - read by the render script and the app.

framing.composition: subject in the lower two thirds, calm uncluttered space in the upper third where the slide's headline and caption sit - the image must never compete with the copy
framing.safe_area: keep the top 28% and bottom 18% visually quiet: the headline sits above, the button below

_revision_note: Rewritten 2026-07-30 (owner): the render had him sitting ON A BED with a phone, smiling at it - the same lounging imagery rejected on slide 03, and no study context at all. Cause: the prompt named a FRAMING ('close three-quarter view') but never a SETTING, so the model chose one, and an unspecified teenager with a phone becomes a teenager on a bed. Now seated upright at a kitchen table with an open exercise book and pen in frame, and bed/bedroom/idle-scrolling are in the negative prompt. Lesson: name the setting on every slide, even a tight crop - especially a tight crop, since the little that IS visible is all the model has to place it.
_casting_note: Cast as a Coloured South African girl of about 16 (owner, 2026-07-30). The prompts said only 'a South African teenager'/'parent', so the model defaulted and EVERY slide came back Black and male. The onboarding carousel is the first thing anyone sees on a national platform - a learner should be able to find themselves in it. students/01 and students/04 keep their approved casting; majority representation is right, it just cannot be the only representation.
_home_note: A person and their house travel together (owner, 2026-07-30). Slides 03 and 04 came back as two different-looking boys in the SAME bedroom - same desk, same shelf, same shirt on the same hook, different hair. Either it is one child, consistent down to the hair, or it is a different child in a DIFFERENT HOME. Every slide now names a home that no other slide uses.
